  ✗ [FC-001] Factual Correctness: Omission of common spelling rules for adding '-ed' to regular verbs. (flagged 2 times)
  ✗ [CC-001] Clarity & Communication: Lack of additional examples of regular verbs in the simple past tense. (flagged 2 times)
  ✗ [DC-001] Depth & Completeness: Failure to mention irregular verbs and their unique past tense forms. (flagged 2 times)

generated_text:
To make simple past tense sentences in English, you add the suffix "-ed" to the base form of a regular verb. Common rules for adding "-ed" include: "walk" becomes "walked", "run" becomes "ran", and "eat" becomes "ate". The sentence structure is: Subject + Past Verb + Object. Example: "I walked to the store."

It's important to note that there are irregular verbs that do not follow the "-ed" rule. Examples include: "go" becomes "went", "see" becomes "saw", and "take" becomes "took".
